name: Priscilla

best_quote.text: apostolo uenisse aut in Montano et Priscilla, sicut Cataphryges

namesake_notes: Priscilla wife of Aquila (Acts, Rom 16, 1 Cor 16) in all Chrysostom and Augustine Acts quotations; not the Montanist.
editorial_notes: Seven Councils notes on Basil/Tillemont and Montanus with Priscilla and Maximilla (editor); Tertullian Oehler index lines; Hippolytus table of contents/summaries.
comment: Montanist Priscilla appears only in Augustine De agone (one passage, in several editions) within the Latin pastoral shelf. Latin apologists mentions (Tertullian De monogamia/De ieiunio/Adv Prax, Hippolytus Refutation) lie outside the shelved works (Commodian, Cyprian Ad Demetrianum, Tertullian De anima/Ad martyras), so U. Round-1 S counts in imperial-juridical were editorial notes, not S.

name: Arnobius of Sicca

namesake_notes: The Nestorius file (Loofs) discusses "Arnobius junior", the 5th-century author of the Conflictus Arnobii cum Serapione, a different person, in German scholarly prose. Van Braght quotes Arnobius "in Psalms 146" (really Arnobius the Younger commentary on Psalms) and dates him A.D. 300, so he conflates the two; counted S only because the tradition names the A.D. 300 Arnobius, flagged.
editorial_notes: Loofs introduction and apparatus on Nestorius counted E/N. Jerome letters LVIII, LX, LXII (npnf206) and the Illustrious Men endnote (npnf203) are other works than the shelved Against Jovinianus and Apology, so U.
comment: Round-1 count of 5 for hieronymian came from Jerome Letters and Illustrious Men, which are not the shelved works; only the Chronicle entry is S. Anabaptist reaches at most 4 distinct passages (two A.D. 300/301 blocks of van Braght commentary on the same quotations) and rests on a conflation of two Arnobii.

namesake_notes: Dominant namesake: Evagrius Scholasticus (historian of Epiphania), named by Mansi/Migne notes, Walford introduction, Kihn, Liberatus editor; also Evagrius of Antioch (Paulinus schism) in Michael tome 2, Severus letters, Kihn; Evagrius the philosopher in Moschus Pratum (letter to Synesius).
editorial_notes: Walford biographical introduction; Migne editorial footnotes and Baronius citations in Liberatus (lines 75033-86375) and in the Dorotheus file; Kugener, Nau and Chabot footnotes; Kihn German introduction; Chalcedon introductory note.
comment: Not a pass. Contexts given (sample of totals) show only 1 clean passage each for Syriac and Judean desert; Michael 59025 "Evagrius dit: Dieu est simple" left U (which Evagrius unclear); Dorotheus Doctrinae and Climacus lie outside the Barsanuphius locus; Moschus 28908/29629 lie beyond the locus (~25000). My own grep: Evagrius Scholasticus (Walford 9529, 9724) names Evagrius Ponticus only twice, and Michael tome 1 line 60795 is a further unlisted Ponticus mention, so neither tradition nears 5.

comment: Only one tradition reaches 5, so passes is false. Welsh: Annales Cambriae shelf locus is only the 768 Easter entry, so the 521/562/597 entries (2399, 2417, 2516) are outside it, labelled U.

name: Ilarion of Kyiv
namesake_notes: Hilarion archbishop of Riazan (17th c., Nikon trial, Ligarides) in all Russian contexts; St Hilarion of Gaza (4th c. hermit) in the Roman Breviary and in the Petit/Patrologia Orientalis 15 Vita.
editorial_notes: Ligarides footnotes by Palmer (2163 style bracketed notes) also present but irrelevant as all are namesakes.
comment: No mention of Ilarion of Kyiv (11th c.) in any sampled context; all contexts are other Hilarions. Does not reach any tradition at 5.

namesake_notes: Biblical Job (book of Job, citations "Job xxii. 21" etc.) dominates the Methodist, Quaker and Evangelical Awakening contexts; also Job Chilaway, Job Johnson, Job Pugh, Rev. Job Strong; in Mouravieff: Job of Kyiv (Boretsky, 8207), Job metropolitan of Novgorod (12177) and Job bishop of Suzdal (13511 second mention) are other men; Philaret catechism cites the book of Job.
editorial_notes: Wesley Journal (Curnock) footnotes and Brainerd/Edwards title-page and contents matter where the contexts carry Job references; none counted.
comment: Only the Russian synodal-century tradition reaches 5 (Mouravieff on Patriarch Job; 13511 counted via the same passage naming "Job metropolitan of All Russia"), so passes is false. The other three are biblical or other namesakes in every context of the sample.
